body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not allow CCDF enrollment of children experiencing homelessness while the required eligibility documentation is obtained, as required by 98.51(a). (Plan Question 2.3.3a) • The Lead Agency does not have a grace period for children who are in foster care or children experiencing homelessness to receive CCDF assistance while providing their families with a reasonable time to take any necessary actions to comply with immunizations and other health and safety requirements and did not establish the length of the grace period in consultation with the State public health agency, as required by 94.41(a)(1)(i)(C). (Plan Questions 2.3.3bi and 2.3.3bii) Overall Target Completion Date: 10/01/2024 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 After consulting with the Mississippi State Department of Health (MSDH), the lead agency will allow children experiencing homelessness a 10-business day grace period to receive documentation . The grace period will begin the date the child's subsidy voucher is approved for services in a child care facility that provides CCDF subsidy assistance. 10/01/2024 2 Families who wish to receive CCDF subsidy assistance may contact the MSDH Office of Immunizations directly during this two week grace period to receive proof of immunizations (i.e., a 121 Immunization Form or 122 Form) once the request has been made to MSDH by the family. 10/01/2024

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not pay all provider types prospectively or alternatively does not demonstrate that it is not a generally-accepted practice for all provider types, as required by 98.45(m)(1). body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency has not established a standard for the administration of medication, consistent with standards for parental consent, for license-exempt centers, license- exempt family child care providers, or license-exempt in-home providers, as required by 98.41(a)(1)(iii). (Plan Questions 5.3.3aiv, 5.3.3av, 5.3.3avi, 5.3.3biv, 5.3.3bv, and 5.3.3bvi) • The Lead Agency does not require an annual inspection for license-exempt centers or license-exempt family child care providers for compliance with an enforceable standard for administration of medication consistent with standards for parental consent, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(ii). (Plan Questions 5.5.2ai and 5.5.2bi) Overall Target Completion Date: 03/01/2025 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 License-exempt centers, including family child care providers, were notified per Attorney General opinion they would be ineligible for subsidy until all licensing requirements were met. License exempt centers, not including family child care providers, met the May 1, 2024 deadline and are being monitored bi- annually. 2 MS State Department of Health (MSDH) Staff trained on new Family Child Care regulations and monitoring tool. 10/29/2024 3 MSDH Regulations Governing Licensure of Family Child Care (Five or Fewer Children) Regulations approved by the MS State Board of Health. body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency did not sufficiently describe fiscal controls that allow for tracking of funds to establish allowable expenditures, as required by 98.67(c)(2). (Plan Question 10.1.2b) Overall Target Completion Date: 10/01/2024 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 The MDHS Division of Early Childhood Care & Development (DECCD), which is the division that oversees the CCDF program, has a finance team (two business managers and a finance director) that solely oversee CCDF fiscal spending and activities. This team utilizes both Smartsheet reporting functions and the and the Mississippi Accountability System for Government Information and Collaboration (MAGIC) to to track spending for all CCDF activities. To account for and track CCDF spending activities a code is assigned to the transaction. Codes are broken down by CCDF fiscal year and spending activity (i.e., direct services, indirect services, quality improvement, infant/toddler, administrative costs, etc.) A code is assigned to each invoice when it is processed. That code determines which year and category that transaction will fall under. Transactions are recorded in Smartsheet and are reconciled each month against the MAGIC CCDF ledger to make sure every transaction that has been approved is accounted for properly. 10/01/2024 2 To ensure accuracy of spending and reporting within each CCDF activity category, the DECCD Finance Director reviews and compares the MAGIC monthly transaction report/ledger with each transaction that is recorded on the DECCD CCDF Smartsheet. Throughout each month as invoices are coded and approved to be paid. The 10/01/2024 Finance Director flags any expenses on the MAGIC ledger that do not match the Smartsheet report. Each month, the DECCD team meets with the lead agency's larger Budgets and Accounting Division leadership to discuss mismatched transactions on the report and works with the larger division to correct any discrepancies. 3 The lead agency utilizes subgrantee agreements with quality partners to perform some CCDF quality improvement activities. Quality partners submit reimbursement claims monthly that must be reviewed and approved in a timely manner. Our Business managers receive notification when a claim has been submitted through a Smartsheet program. The lead agency follows a five business day time frame to review the claims and process them for payment. DECCD business managers review claims for amounts and spending categories and compare against each subgrantee contract and budget. The team also reviews all supporting documentation to guarantee funds are spent appropriately. If any errors are found, the business team will notify the respective quality partner through the CCDF Smartsheet that corrections must be made and the claim must be resubmitted. Once everything is correct, the DECCD Division Director/CCDF Administrator will review, sign, and approve the claim to be paid. This claim is then sent to the subgrantee analyst and manager in the lead agency's Budgets and Accounting division to process the claim through MAGIC for payment. 10/01/2024
